leaderboard.description: Empirical-Bayes Gamma-Poisson day-of-week rates with shrinkage.
leaderboard.assumptions: Weekday rates are draws from a common population.
leaderboard.fails_when: A weekday is genuinely unlike the others; shrinkage over-corrects.

leaderboard.description: Negative Binomial on day-of-week plus a linear weekly trend.
leaderboard.assumptions: As negbin-glm, plus a steady drift in level.
leaderboard.fails_when: The trend is extrapolated past where it holds.

leaderboard.description: Three-state HMM; Poisson emissions with an overdispersion correction.
leaderboard.assumptions: As poisson-hmm, with extra scatter inside each regime.
leaderboard.fails_when: States are poorly separated; the extra freedom just absorbs noise.

leaderboard.description: SARIMA(1,0,1)x(1,0,1,7) on log1p(counts).
leaderboard.assumptions: Log counts are approximately Gaussian with weekly seasonality.
leaderboard.fails_when: Zeros and extreme spikes — log1p tames them but does not make them Gaussian.

leaderboard.description: Hidden Markov Model with Poisson emissions; 2-3 latent activity states.
leaderboard.assumptions: A small number of discrete, persistent activity regimes.
leaderboard.fails_when: Activity varies continuously rather than in discrete modes.

leaderboard.description: Linear opinion pool over member models (mixture of predictive densities).
leaderboard.assumptions: Members are individually reasonable; disagreement is real uncertainty.
leaderboard.fails_when: One member is badly wrong — the pool inherits its tail.

leaderboard.description: Quantile-averaged (Vincentized) combination of member models.
leaderboard.assumptions: Members share a shape; their disagreement is mostly about level.
leaderboard.fails_when: Members are genuinely bimodal — averaging quantiles invents a middle.

leaderboard.description: Log-linear count autoregression with a persistent conditional rate.
leaderboard.assumptions: Today's rate depends on yesterday's count and yesterday's rate.
leaderboard.fails_when: Bursts are near-instantaneous within a day rather than across days.

leaderboard.description: Negative Binomial (NB2) regression on day-of-week.
leaderboard.assumptions: Rate varies day to day around a weekday mean; days independent.
leaderboard.fails_when: Bursts run across consecutive days — it has no memory.

leaderboard.description: Resamples each remaining day independently — the no-clustering control.
leaderboard.assumptions: Days within a week are independent given the weekday.
leaderboard.fails_when: Bursts span days, which is precisely what it cannot represent.

leaderboard.description: Resamples each remaining weekday from its own historical values.
leaderboard.assumptions: Days are exchangeable within a weekday; no trend, no memory.
leaderboard.fails_when: The level shifts, or activity clusters across days within a week.

leaderboard.description: Zero-inflated Negative Binomial: structural zeros plus overdispersion.
leaderboard.assumptions: Both mechanisms operate — off-days and a wandering rate.
leaderboard.fails_when: Thin data; the two mechanisms compete to explain the same zeros.

leaderboard.description: Resamples the intact remainder-of-week as a single block.
leaderboard.assumptions: Within-week clustering is a stable feature of the process.
leaderboard.fails_when: The level shifts; blocks from an old regime mislead.

leaderboard.description: Hawkes process with exponential kernel and a circadian background.
leaderboard.assumptions: Posts trigger further posts; the effect decays exponentially.
leaderboard.fails_when: Bursts are actually driven by outside events — indistinguishable here.

leaderboard.description: Median of the last 4 complete weeks, apportioned over remaining days.
leaderboard.assumptions: The recent level is the best guess; weekday shares are stable.
leaderboard.fails_when: A regime change happened inside the 4-week window.

leaderboard.description: As empirical-dow, but only the last 8 weeks.
leaderboard.assumptions: Recent behaviour is more relevant than old behaviour.
leaderboard.fails_when: Eight weeks is too thin to see the tail; tail estimates get soft.

leaderboard.description: Log-linear Poisson regression on day-of-week.
leaderboard.assumptions: Fixed rate per weekday; posts independent; variance == mean.
leaderboard.fails_when: Always here — the data is wildly overdispersed. Kept as the reference failure.

leaderboard.description: Zero-inflated Poisson: a structural-zero switch, then a count.
leaderboard.assumptions: A fraction of days are 'off' entirely; the rest are Poisson.
leaderboard.fails_when: Overdispersion comes from bursts rather than from zeros.

leaderboard.description: LightGBM quantile regression over calendar and lag features.
leaderboard.assumptions: Recent history and the calendar carry the signal; enough rows to learn from.
leaderboard.fails_when: Data is thin, or the pattern it learned has since changed.

leaderboard.description: Last week's total, with the historical week-over-week change distribution.
leaderboard.assumptions: Consecutive weeks are similar; changes are stationary.
leaderboard.fails_when: Volume is trending, or last week was itself an outlier.

notes: Every pre-registered model is listed, including those that lost badly.
CRPS is the primary metric; lower is better and it is in units of posts.
Skill is measured against climatology (empirical-dow): 0.10 means 10% of its error removed.
coverage80 should be ~0.80. Much below means overconfident intervals.
PIT p-value below 0.05 means the forecast distribution is NOT calibrated.
The holdout leaderboard is the honest number; the main one was visible during development.
